content: Magnesium gluconate is a medication used to treat low levels of magnesium in the blood. Low magnesium levels can result from gastrointestinal disorders, prolonged vomiting or diarrhea, kidney disease, or other medical conditions. Certain medications can also lower magnesium levels. This drug may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Magnesium gluconate is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral use. It is typically taken two to four times daily, depending on your specific condition. Follow the instructions on your prescription or package label carefully. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take this medication exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. To minimize side effects, take magnesium gluconate with meals. If you are using an extended-release tablet, do not chew or crush it. However, some tablets may be crushed and mixed with food; consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Before starting magnesium gluconate, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other magnesium-containing products, tetracycline (e.g., Achromycin V, Panmycin, Sumycin), digoxin (Lanoxin), nitrofurantoin (e.g., Furadantin, Macrobid, Macrodantin), penicillamine (e.g., Cuprimine, Depen Titratable), and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease, stomach problems, or intestinal disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. A well-balanced diet typically provides sufficient magnesium. However, supplements may be necessary in cases of illness or medication use. Magnesium is naturally found in foods such as green leafy vegetables, nuts, peas, beans, and whole grains. A high-fat diet can reduce magnesium absorption, and overcooking food can also decrease magnesium content. Follow the dietary recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. If you miss a dose of magnesium gluconate, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Magnesium gluconate may cause side effects. Minor side effects include diarrhea and stomach upset. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include stomach cramps, vomiting, flushing of the skin, dizziness, and severe upset stomach. If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store magnesium gluconate in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly; consult your pharmacist for disposal instructions. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to magnesium gluconate. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Magnesium gluconate is sold under brand names such as Almora®, Magtrate®, and Magonate®.
